data.name: Alphadia Genesis
data.detailed_description:
Alphadia Genesis chronicles an epic adventure with Fray and his investigative team from the Archleign Kingdom as they set out to solve a mysterious murder case in a nearby city. After some initial investigations, Fray and his companions are joined by delegates from the Ghalzabine Kingdom.

This causes tensions to run high, as the Archleign and Ghalzabine Kingdoms have shared an uneasy relationship since the clone-centric ‘Energi War’ 15 years prior to the joint investigation.

Twists and turns lie await as Fray and his fellow investigators soon discover that there may be more than meets the eye with this particular case...

Built for Steam!
Expect exclusive trading cards, badges, backgrounds as well as fully redesigned controls for PC gamers... this really is the best way to play Alphadia Genesis.

Characters you care for!
Each character has their own distinct personality, and this helps to create a strong bond between the player and the heroes of Lagoon. In addition to this, many of the game’s characters are voiced by leading Japanese voice actors - giving them even more depth and making the world of Lagoon even more immerse.

The Best of Both Dimensions!
While Fray and co. are exploring Lagoon, Alphadia Genesis has a wonderful 16-bit style reminiscent of classic JRPGs of old... on the battlefield however it’s a whole different story. With fully animated 3D battles, the turn-based action really comes to life.

More than Meets the Eye!
The plot of Alphadia Genesis is packed with twists and turns - you’ll need to stay on your toes to keep up.

Not a-Fray-ed to laugh!
While the plot is serious - there are plenty of funny moments too... watch out for the lickers!

reviews.review:
A surprisingly well done RPG that doesn't quite become great due to the weak dungeon designs and mediocre overworld graphics, but is still definitely worth playing due to some interesting combat mechanics that evolve very interestingly as you progress. The story isn't nonsensical but I couldn't even get a grip on the plot until about halfway through... it's about science fiction clones, which is weird because the game takes place in a fantasy world with kings and castles.

The joy in Alphadia Genesis is leveling, getting new skills and abilities and changing your tactics to proceed. You can't keep doing the same thing the entire game because enemies gradually get stronger and start instakilling you and your newly unlocked abilities have slight nuance to them to give you a bit of an edge to win. The first half of this game is a joke, but the middle section is tough. It then gets obscenely difficult at the end. I was level 80 and I had to attempt the final boss about a dozen times before I killed it.

You have six characters and there's a lot of freedom on how to set up your party. The post-game stuff was the most fun to me. There are a bunch of optional boss fights that eventually grant you legendary weapons and armor. There are other side quests throughout, but they aren't necessary and don't give you much in terms of useful rewards. The achievements are granted simply for finishing the game, except for one that requires you to open all 220 chests in the game.

This is where I like the game a little less because the dungeon designs through most of the game are super dull. Most dungeons are just straight lines to the boss at the end with cracks in the wall denoting passages that lead to chests. While you try to locate the chests the random encounters constantly interrupt the gameplay which is super annoying. You can escape every battle with 100% accuracy and the game will let you retry if you die (Along with saving anywhere) so in that sense it's overly forgiving, but you do still need to adopt the correct strategy to win and this can be quite tough.

I only stopped to grind a few times in the game and grinding as a whole is not that difficult. This is a 20-25 hour JRPG with a not-so-great story but great character dialogue. It reminds me a bit of Lunar: Silver Star Story in that sense because the interpersonal conversations between the characters are well done despite the overarching narrative being kinda bleh. The music is great and so are the combat graphics. Between status effects, different abilities, a magic system that upgrades with equipped rings and different equipment adjustments it has much more depth than your average JRPG, but it's hard not to notice the flaws if you've beaten a lot of these games. You get a puzzle extremely rarely and there's little interactivity. The final dungeon has key cards you need to hunt down and I wondered why the whole game wasn't like that. I think back to classic JRPGs like FF7 and Wild Arms on PS1, wherein the dungeon element has an element of surprise or mechanics that make it interesting to explore and figure out. If you can see past that there's a lot of value here and it's a totally fine indie JRPG that's worth trying if you like the genre. It just needed to drop the "generic RPG" template and show its personality more in terms of visual, story and dungeon design.
